name: Macao Pidgin Portuguese
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Araujo, Gabriel Antunes de & Yuxin Bian. 2026. Algumas contribuições do Cantonês para o Pidgin Maquista de Macau. Cadernos de Estudos Linguísticos (Campinas) 68: 1-17, e026013. DOI 10.20396/cel.v68i00.8683027
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sec. 3.1 and 4 (pp. 7, 10-11): the Chinese-character transcriptions in the Ao Yi list (1751) and the Compendium use different homophonous characters for strong (tonic) vs weak (atonic) syllables, e.g. 巴喇罷 *pɑː.lɑː.pɑː 'barba' with 巴 = tonic and 罷 = atonic (following Liu 2025); but the authors state explicitly that 'ainda não é possível descrever o sistema acentual do PMM' (it is not yet possible to describe the stress system of MPM). Also notes no prior work has described PMM phonology systematically. No statement of where stress falls.

sources.citation: Hu Huiming 胡慧明. 2004. 《澳門記略》反映的澳門土生葡語面貌 [The facet of the Portuguese dialect of Macau in Aomen Jilüe]. 文化雜誌 Review of Culture (Chinese edition) 52: 51-98.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Discusses segmental correspondences of the 395-item Ao Yi glossary (1751) vs Portuguese/Macanese; mentions stress only incidentally (stressed e realized [i], unstressed o > u, as in Macanese), presupposing Portuguese stress positions; no statement of where stress falls in the pidgin.

sources.citation: Zhang Wenqin 章文欽. 2008. 廣東葡語初探 [A preliminary investigation of Canton Portuguese]. 文化雜誌 Review of Culture (Chinese edition) 68: 1-17.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Historical account of the pidgin ('Canton Portuguese'), its users and Chinese-character glossaries; no phonology, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Liu Yuelian 劉月蓮. 2004. 《澳門記略》附錄〈澳譯〉初探 [A preliminary study of the appendix Ao Yi of Aomen Jilüe]. 文化雜誌 Review of Culture (Chinese edition) 52: 99-120.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Philological study of which Chinese variety (Cantonese/Min/Mandarin) underlies the character transcriptions; mentions Chinese tones of transcription characters only; nothing on Portuguese-pidgin word stress.

sources.citation: Thompson, Robert Wallace. 1959. Two synchronic cross-sections in the Portuguese dialect of Macao. Orbis 8: 29-53 [read in the Chinese translation by Hu Huiming, 兩份同期澳門葡語方言資料比較研究, Review of Culture (Chinese ed.) 68 (2008): 18-37].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Gives consonant/vowel inventory of modern (1950s Hong Kong) Macanese Creole and compares the 1751 Ao Yi glossary item by item; modern forms are cited with stress marks (e.g. [ˈvelo], [ˈfilo]) but there is no rule statement, and nothing on stress in the 18th-c. pidgin material.

sources.citation: Li, Michelle & Stephen Matthews. 2016. An outline of Macau Pidgin Portuguese. Journal of Pidgin and Creole Languages 31(1): 141-183.

sources.note: The fullest modern description (43 pp.) of the pidgin, with a section on transcription practices of the Compendium; the most likely place for any remark on stress/phonology recoverable from the character transcriptions.
